summary: Resume duplication and partial-final-choice when SSE streams are proxied over HTTP/2 multiplexed connections
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent duplication of the last streamed segment and a truncated final choice after client-triggered reconnects when SSE is proxied through an HTTP/2 multiplexing path. The client receives a duplicate mid-sentence fragment followed immediately by an end event that omits the last few words.

Impact: Affects real-time UX for Acme's live summarization feature. Customers see duplicated words and cut-off sentences ~1-3% of long (>10k token) streams. Reported in production us-east region and causing apparent hallucination-like artifacts in final outputs (customer counts these as correctness failures).

Environment: prod / us-east behind CDN/edge + ALB -> Envoy ingress -> serving runtime. Observed with SSE (text/event-stream) over HTTP/2 multiplexed connections from edge to internal proxies. Affected models: redwood-14b-v1 (rt-compat) and redwood-7b-v1 in heavy token flows.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Initiate a long streaming generation via SSE from a browser client (keep-alive manifest every 25s).
2) Induce a fast reconnect on the client (switching mobile network or forced websocket fallback).
3) Client sends resume token with last-event-id header.
4) On ~10-20% of reconnects the client receives an extra duplicate fragment (e.g., previous 3 words repeated) then an end event that is missing the final 2-6 words.

Observed logs / snippets (sanitized):
- Server stream before disconnect:
  data: {"id":"evt-50123","choice":0,"delta":"...the quick brown fox jumped"}
  data: {"id":"evt-50124","choice":0,"delta":" over the lazy"}
  data: {"id":"evt-50125","choice":0,"delta":" dog.\n"}
- After client reconnect & resume request (last-event-id: evt-50125):
  data: {"id":"evt-50125","choice":0,"delta":" dog."}   <-- duplicate fragment received
  data: {"id":"evt-50126","choice":0,"delta":"\n"}       <-- end event received but final commentary truncated

Additional context: Acme runs multiple parallel SSE sessions per browser tab, and their edge uses HTTP/2 connection pooling to origin to reduce connections. Hypothesis from customer: HTTP/2 stream reuse and server-side resume reconciliation are occasionally replaying a buffered fragment during stream reattach.

Attachments: client-side HAR, server side trace IDs (traces: trace-us-east-001234, trace-us-east-001237), CDN edge request IDs provided in comments.

2026-03-11 09:33 - Jonas Müller (SRE): Found pattern in traces: connection pool reused the same HTTP/2 connection and stream IDs were remapped by edge -> origin translation, there are 503 precondition resets logged immediately prior to reconnects for the affected traces. Collecting more stream-level debug logs from envoy.

2026-03-12 15:47 - Riley Ortiz (Eng): Reproduced locally using synthetic HTTP/2 multiplexing test harness. Observed race where buffered SSE event chunk is in-flight in the ALB->envoy stream and server resume handler emits the same event again when the client re-subscribes. Hypothesis: a race between stream buffer flush and resume ACK path leads to duplicate delivery.

2026-03-13 08:05 - Maya Patel (Support): Notified customer of investigation. Recommended temporary mitigation: set client-side dedupe on last 2 SSE events and increase heartbeat to 5s to reduce edge idle preconditions. Customer accepted temporary workaround.

2026-03-13 12:22 - Jonas Müller (SRE): Proposed long-term fix: add idempotent resume handshake (server-to-client resume-ack with last-seen-sequence) and tighten stream buffer flush ordering in ingress. Opening infra ticket INT-3399 to roll envoy hotfix.
investigation_notes: Collected HAR, server traces, and CDN logs for the affected sessions (trace-us-east-001234, trace-us-east-001237).
Reproducer created that mirrors customer topology (HTTP/2 multiplexing, keepalive heartbeats, forced client reconnect during buffer flush).

Observed duplicate delivery when ALB reports stream RESET before origin sees final buffer flush; origin resume logic re-emits last buffer chunk based on last persisted offset rather than stream-ack state.
Observed higher incidence when multiple SSEs share a single upstream HTTP/2 connection (multiplexing > 4), suggesting a pool/reuse race condition.

Hypothesis: mismatch between last-event-id-based resume offset and transient network-level resets causes server to conservatively re-send the last chunk, but a partial in-flight chunk on the client side is also delivered leading to duplication and truncated final choice when the end marker is processed earlier.
Risk assessment: moderate for long sessions; likely to surface only on proxied HTTP/2 paths with aggressive connection pooling or ingress that does stream ID translation.

Next steps: unit test for resume path, implement resume-ack protocol extension, deploy Envoy config change to reduce aggressive stream reuse for SSE traffic, and add server-side dedupe for last N tokens when resume occurs.
resolution_notes: Workaround deployed: Support recommended client-side dedupe and increased keepalive; customer accepted. Infra change INT-3399 created to patch envoy config to avoid stream reuse for SSE traffic and a server-side change scheduled to add resume-ack and dedupe logic in the serving runtime. Monitoring dashboards updated to track SSE resume duplication rate. Pending rollout of code changes and post-deploy verification.
